analysis: The supplied units are base-side test text from EngineV2BridgeTests.swift (lines 1870-3127). They cover shared-KV budget reservation and release, lookup receipts, request-id hardening, seeded sampling ids, the logprobs cap and paged KV. According to the file_changes map (range_map_complete=true), none of these lines changed. Base-side changes are limited to line 153. Head-side changes are at 146-147, 155, 440, 459 and 811-896. The head-side changes add the test-only tokenizer decodeTable and plumb stopStringScope into makeBridge. They also add tests for EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence with a model-scoped stop-string scope (gpt-oss channel analysis vs. final). These changes are test code only. They do not alter the T-041 cache-salt scoping, the SSD HMAC naming, or the staging-reservation release paths. The surrounding tests at base lines 2067-2324 still assert that reservations are released on rejection, teardown and shutdown. Lines 2752-2854 assert that cacheSalt is preserved per scope. No security regression is visible in the test diff. Integration should check the production change in EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence and ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope, which this batch does not include. If stop-scope matching mishandles the analysis/final channel boundary, analysis-channel text could be surfaced or truncated incorrectly. That would be an output-correctness concern for A-001 and T-007, not a plaintext-leak path. This is noted as an integration question, not a finding.
